criteria.rationale: The delete_expired method calculates retention based on draft_timestamp instead of receipt_timestamp. Line 44 uses 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now' to determine expiration, but the legal rule requires the retention period to begin at the receipt timestamp, not the draft timestamp. The receipt_timestamp is captured and stored (lines 13, 25, 30) but never used in the retention calculation. The 7-day period (RETENTION_PERIOD constant at line 6) is correct, but it is applied to the wrong timestamp. Exhaustive search confirmed no alternative receipt-timestamp-based deletion path exists in the repository.

The notice_text is stored without modification. The receive method accepts notice_text as a parameter and stores it directly in the Notice dataclass (line 30) without any transformation, stripping, sanitization, or removal of content. The dataclass field is frozen (line 9), preventing post-creation modification. No text processing logic exists anywhere in the repository. The schema defines notice_text as TEXT NOT NULL, preserving the full content. Exhaustive search for text modification patterns found no matches.

decision.rationale: The service is offered to the public per confirmed operator fact (factId 35c3fde5-32f6-4d2b-b67b-ad8dbe08e99c). The repository implements a notice service that stores notice records with text, receipt timestamps, and other metadata. Private household use is excluded per the legal rule, and this is a public deployment. Temporary test records are handled via the is_temporary_test flag and excluded from retention processing as permitted by Article 3 exception.

recommendations: Change line 44 in service.py from 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now' to 'notice.receipt_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now' to calculate expiration from the legally required receipt timestamp.
Add unit tests verifying that retention periods are calculated from receipt_timestamp, not draft_timestamp, including scenarios where these timestamps differ significantly.
Consider adding validation to ensure receipt_timestamp is not after the current time when records are received, as receipt should occur at or before the system processes the notice.
findings.summary: NON_COMPLIANT. The service has a critical defect in retention period calculation. The delete_expired method uses draft_timestamp instead of receipt_timestamp to determine when records expire (line 44: 'notice.draft_timestamp + RETENTION_PERIOD <= now'). This violates the legal requirement that the 7-day retention period must begin at receipt, not draft time. The receipt_timestamp is captured and stored but never used in expiration logic. Text preservation is compliant: notice_text is stored without modification in a frozen dataclass, with no sanitization or content removal logic detected. Temporary test records are correctly excluded from retention processing via the is_temporary_test flag.

summary: This assessment evaluated a public-facing notice service against statutory retention requirements. The service stores notice records with text, receipt timestamps, draft timestamps, and test-record flags. One engineering rule was assessed (ER-RETENTION-DUTY: Notice Record Retention) covering 7-day retention requirements and text preservation duties. The service is NON_COMPLIANT due to a critical implementation error in the retention calculation logic. While the service correctly preserves notice text without modification (criterion C-2 MET), it incorrectly calculates the retention period from the draft timestamp instead of the legally required receipt timestamp (criterion C-1 NOT_MET). The 7-day retention period constant is correctly defined, but is applied to the wrong timestamp field in the delete_expired method.
